Comedian Michael McIntyre joined prominent figures including Dame Helen Mirren, Hugh Grant and Bill Nighy to support charities remembering the victims of 9/11.

They gathered on the Boston Consulting Group (BCG) trading floor in Canary Wharf on Friday for an annual charity day honouring 658 colleagues lost on September 11, 2001.

Actor Tom Hardy, DJ Fatboy Slim, Little Mix star Leigh-Anne Pinnock and former England manager Sir Gareth Southgate were among the attendees.

Participating on behalf of Prostate Cancer Research, McIntyre urged men over 50 to get checked.

He said: “It’s a very simple message.

open image in gallery Hugh Grant on the trading floor ( PA )

“Once you turn 50 you have a very big chance of getting what is a silent killer.

“You do not know that you have it. There are no symptoms, so the only thing you can do is test for it and once you hit 50, it’s very important that you do that because one in eight people actually do get this.

“I had a test, a PSA (prostate-specific antigen) test. You can get it from your doctor. The NHS will give it to you. You need to ask for it, and then you can rule that out and have a nice day.

“A friend of mine had it last year, I couldn’t believe how serious it is, a dangerous it is, and how easy it is to prevent it. And the last thing anybody wants is for this to happen, knowing that it could have been prevented.”

The PSA test can indicate prostate conditions including prostate cancer or an enlarged prostate.

High levels may be a sign of a prostate condition, such as an enlarged prostate, or prostate cancer.

The PSA test is not used in routine NHS screening because it is not yet reliable enough to detect prostate cancer that needs treatment.

open image in gallery Leigh-Anne Pinnock takes a call ( PA )

Launched in 2005, the BCG Charity Day has since raised more than 234 million dollars (£173 million) for hundreds of charities around the world.

The global revenues and broker commissions from the day goes to 60 participating charities including Caudwell Youth, the Mayor’s Fund for London, Saint Francis Hospice, Greenhouse Sports and When You Wish Upon a Star.

Former footballer Jamie Redknapp also joined the trading floor in support of the Laureus Sport for Good, an organisation which offers children around the world opportunities to try different sports.

Redknapp said this type of access to sport could help “change lives”.

He told PA: “I think that’s why it’s so important to me, because I’ve been so lucky.

open image in gallery Former footballer Jamie Redknapp also joined the trading floor in support of the Laureus Sport for Good ( PA )

“I think we all recognise how good sports been for us and it’s nice to give a little bit back as well.

“I come from obviously a loving family. Not everyone is fortunate enough to have those opportunities. So charities like Laureus in 300 different countries, 300 different opportunities for people in you know all different parts of the world.

“It’s a fantastic charity and I’m super proud to be working for them.

“They do a really good job.”

On being a trader full-time, he added: “I wouldn’t want to do it for a living. It’s too pressurised for me.”

Broadcaster Kate Garraway also joined the trading floor along with comedian Keith Lemon and Coronation Street star Ellie Leach.

Other charities represented on the day included Help for Heroes, the John Terry Foundation, Muscular Dystrophy UK, Action Medical Research and Action for Children.

BGC’s co-chief executive Sean Windeatt said: “I remember being on the phone and the line just went dead. You never forget a moment like that.

“We lost more than 650 friends and colleagues that day, and everything we have built since has been done in their memory.

“Our first job was looking after their families. Then it fell to London to help rebuild the business, and out of that came the idea of taking something so tragic and building something lasting from it.”

News.title: iPhone Duo vs Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: How the flagflip foldables compare
News.content:
Sign up to our free weekly IndyTech newsletter delivered straight to your inbox Sign up to our free IndyTech newsletter Sign up to our free IndyTech newsletter Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Samsung has had an eight-year head start on Apple in making foldable phones. But after years of rumours, Apple has finally entered the ring, and it’s taking aim at the South Korean tech giant.

Announced on 9 September, the iPhone Duo is Apple’s first foldable iPhone, and in form factor alone, it’s a direct rival to the recently launched Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8. Boasting a book-style design, it transforms from a regular smartphone into a near-iPad mini-sized device when you unfold it.

But while they might work – conceptually, anyway – in much the same way, Apple and Samsung have presented two very different smartphones in terms of execution. Based on what Apple has announced, I’ve compared the iPhone Duo and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8’s displays, cameras, software, performance, battery life and price.



iPhone Duo Apple’s first-ever foldable iPhone features a 5.4in outer display with a large 7.6in inner screen. It’s expensive and considerably heavier than Samsung’s alternative, but has a flexible hinge, Apple Pencil support and some clever software designed specifically for the folding form factor. It starts from £1,999 and goes on sale in October. Key specifications Outer display: 5.4in OLED, 120Hz

5.4in OLED, 120Hz Inner display: 7.6in OLED, 120Hz

7.6in OLED, 120Hz Processor: A20 Pro

A20 Pro Cameras: 48MP main, 48MP ultrawide

48MP main, 48MP ultrawide Storage: 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, 2TB

256GB, 512GB, 1TB, 2TB Weight: 254g

254g Water and dust resistance: IP68 £1,999 from Very.co.uk Prices may vary

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Samsung’s eighth-generation book-style foldable is slimmer, lighter and £300 cheaper than the iPhone Duo. Like the Duo, it features a passport-style design, and its software is brilliantly polished with picture-perfect folding. I don’t like the lack of a telephoto camera, limited dust protection and lack of S Pen support, however – the latter two you get with the iPhone Duo. It starts at £1,699 for the 256GB model. Key specifications Outer display: 5.5in AMOLED, 120Hz

5.5in AMOLED, 120Hz Inner display: 7.6in AMOLED, 120Hz

7.6in AMOLED, 120Hz Processor: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy

Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy Cameras: 50MP main, 50MP ultrawide

50MP main, 50MP ultrawide Storage: 256GB, 512GB, 1TB

256GB, 512GB, 1TB Weight: 201g

201g Water and dust resistance: IP48 £1,699 from Argos.co.uk Prices may vary

iPhone Duo vs Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Design and displays

It’s a little tricky to know who actually came first when it comes to the passport-sized form factor. While Samsung launched the Galaxy Z Fold 8 a few months before Apple announced the iPhone Duo, it’s been known since early 2025 that Apple was working on a passport-sized book-style foldable.

In any case, they have very similar dimensions. Folded, the iPhone Duo has a 5.4in outer display, with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 featuring a slightly larger 5.5in cover screen. Open them up, though, and both give you a huge 7.6in OLED display, essentially transforming the phones into mini tablets.

But they don’t actually look all that similar. The iPhone Duo has a somewhat controversial asymmetric silhouette. The left side is straight, while the right side is curved, making it look like a “D”. The Samsung Z Fold 8 is all right angles, all the way round.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable phone ( Apple )

Both phones have adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz and can reach up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness.

The most interesting thing is that the iPhone Duo’s inner screen features a nano-texture finish, reducing glare and helping to minimise the visibility of the crease. “From a distance, the display on the inside looks a little darker than a normal iPhone screen. It isn’t, it’s a matte finish that keeps reflections down,” Andrew Griffin said in his first impressions.

While I’ve not tried the iPhone Duo yet, that matte finish does make it look dimmer and duller, though that will have to be tested at a later date. Samsung’s inner display, on the other hand, is glossy like the cover screen. Samsung has put an anti-reflective treatment over the top, with new Flex Titanium technology reinforcing the folding display and helping to reduce the visibility of the crease. Griffin says there’s no visible crease on the Duo at all. While the Z Fold 8 crease is very nearly invisible, you can still see it if you go looking.

Apple has also hidden the selfie camera underneath the Duo’s inner display – and it seems from early coverage that Apple would like users to avoid using that one entirely, using the rear cameras to take selfies instead (more on that below). Samsung, on the other hand, has a conventional 10MP camera embedded in its folding display.

There are differences in the hinges too. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 almost forces you to click it into place when you open it fully to 180 degrees, meaning you can’t prop it open at different angles in the traditional Flex Mode anymore. I found flipping it over and standing it on its edges like a teepee was a way around this.

The Z Fold 8 has more squared-off edges ( Alex Lee/The Independent )

Apple, however, has designed the Duo to work in loads of partially folded positions, so you can fold it into a seated position like a laptop, prop it up on its edges like a tent or fold it like a book.

One of my biggest gripes with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is that both speakers sit on the same half of the phone. Open it up into landscape and they both fire from the left side of the display, so there isn’t much stereo separation when watching videos.

Apple fixes this by placing the iPhone Duo’s two speakers diagonally on opposite halves of the phone. When it’s unfolded, the speakers sit at opposite corners of the display, which should provide much better stereo separation when watching films and TV shows. I’ll need to listen to them myself to see how good they actually sound.

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 does have one pretty huge advantage, however, and that’s the weight. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 weighs just 201g, while the iPhone Duo weighs a hefty 254g. That’s a 53g difference, and given I already found the Fold 8 impressively light for a folding phone, I suspect you’ll notice it.

The iPhone Duo is a lot thicker when shut as well – that’s the first thing that caught my eye when I saw pictures of the device. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 measures 9.7mm when folded and 4.5mm when unfolded. The iPhone Duo is more than 1.5mm thicker when shut (11.3mm folded and 5.2mm unfolded).

That said, the iPhone Duo has much better protection against dust and sand. It has an IP68 rating, while the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is only rated IP48, so you won’t want to take Samsung’s foldable anywhere near the beach.

The iPhone Duo can fold like a laptop ( AFP/Getty )

And, in a slightly bizarre role reversal, Apple is the one offering stylus support. Apple has announced that the iPhone Duo will work with the USB-C Apple Pencil later this year – Samsung dropped S Pen support from the Galaxy Z Fold 8 completely.

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 comes in four colours – lavender, graphite, cream and pistachio – with the latter reserved as a Samsung Store exclusive.

The iPhone Duo only comes in two colours – star white and night sky (black).

Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is a slimmer, lighter foldable, but the iPhone Duo appears to provide a better overall design experience, with a more flexible hinge, better speaker placement, matte inner display and Apple Pencil support, as well as an IP68 rating.

iPhone Duo vs Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Cameras

Both the iPhone Duo and Z Fold 8 feature two rear cameras instead of the triple-camera systems on their respective flagship models.

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 features a 50MP f/1.8 main camera and a 50MP f/1.9 ultrawide. The iPhone Duo is kitted out with a 48MP f/1.6 main camera and a 48MP f/2.2 ultrawide camera. Both feature a 2x optical-quality zoom – no telephoto.

That missing telephoto lens was one of my biggest complaints when I reviewed the Galaxy Z Fold 8. The 2x zoom is perfectly serviceable, but you notice less detail at 5x and 10x digital zoom.

You can barely see the crease on the Z Fold 8 ( Alex Lee/The Independent )

The iPhone Duo may have the same issue. You can shoot at 0.5x, 1x and 2x, and there’s a 10x digital zoom, but there’s no equivalent of the 8x optical-quality zoom on the iPhone 18 Pro. The iPhone Duo’s main camera does at least have a wider f/1.6 aperture, as well as sensor-shift optical image stabilisation, so it might take better-quality low-light photos, but I’ll have to test that.

On the Galaxy Z Fold 8, you can use the cover screen as a viewfinder while taking selfies with the rear cameras. Apple has taken the same idea and pushed it further. The iPhone Duo’s Preview feature puts a live view of the shot on the outer display so the person you’re photographing can frame themselves in the shot, but you can also flip the phone and use the rear cameras for higher-quality selfies, something Apple has been encouraging content creators to do in its demos.

Apple’s also rolled out a Smart Take feature that uses on-device AI to work out when everyone is ready and automatically takes the photo, meaning you don’t have to sprint back into frame after setting a timer. Kid Cue also plays animations on the outer display to persuade children to actually look at the camera.

Samsung has some fun camera tricks too. My FanCam can take a wide landscape video and track one specific person in the frame after the footage is taken, reframing it into a vertical clip for socials.

The iPhone Duo can record 4K Dolby Vision at up to 120fps on its main camera. It also supports Cinematic mode at up to 4K 60fps and can shoot 4K Dolby Vision time-lapses. Samsung can shoot up to 8K video, but it doesn’t have the same Dolby Vision support.

You won’t get a fully-fledged flagship camera experience from either phone. The iPhone Duo might tip the balance on specs alone, however. It has a wider main aperture, better video features and uses the outer display better. Whether it actually takes better pictures, we’ll have to wait to find out.

iPhone Duo vs Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Performance and software

Both phones are powered by the latest flagship chips from Apple and Qualcomm. The iPhone Duo has the same A20 Pro chip found inside the iPhone 18 Pro. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy.

The iPhone Duo only comes in two colours ( Apple )

Apple says the A20 Pro’s six-core CPU is up to 20 per cent faster than the A19 Pro and its seven-core GPU is up to 40 per cent faster and more power efficient. There’s also a new dual 16-core Neural Engine for running Apple Intelligence features on-device. The iPhone Duo also has a vapour chamber to keep everything cool, with Apple claiming up to 35 per cent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro.

I’ve already put the Galaxy Z Fold 8 through its paces, and the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy is seriously quick. Apps open instantly and multitasking is smooth. I haven’t tested the iPhone Duo yet, but given it has the same A20 Pro chip as Apple’s flagship iPhone 18 Pro, I doubt performance is going to be a problem.

Software is much more interesting than the performance specs. Samsung’s had years to perfect how the folding experience works on the Z Fold 8, and it’s brilliant. You can run apps side by side using Multi Window, drag and drop content between them and move seamlessly between the cover and inner displays.

One UI 9’s Multi Window is ultra versatile, and the tech giant’s Galaxy AI Now Nudge feature can recognise what you’re doing and suggest actions in another window, so you don’t need to constantly move between apps.

Apple might be late to the party, but it always does its homework. iOS 27 has been redesigned specifically for the iPhone Duo. The dock and app controls are now on the right side of the phone, making better use of the display (although I’m not sure if this will make it more difficult for lefties to use the phone).

And you can finally multitask on an iPhone. The new Split View lets you run two apps side by side and even save pairs of apps you regularly use together as a single app.

You can prop both up like a tent ( Alex Lee/The Independent )

Apple also demonstrated how Zoom can now show both a presentation and the people on a call; Slack can fit more of your workspace onto the screen; and Netflix can expand across the entire display. Apps also adjust to the position of the hinge, which is fascinating to see, especially in the seated fold position.

One neat thing I’ve spotted from the demonstrations is how much more visually cohesive the experience looks on the iPhone Duo. “That software experience even extends to the process of opening and closing the phone. Apple has done an astonishing job in ensuring that the phone knows it is opening, and mirrors the content on the little screen onto the big one, so that you almost forget they’re not actually the same thing,” Griffin said in his hands-on review. The inner screen on the Z Fold 8, for example, remains black when you start opening it up, only activating when it’s halfway open.

They may be similar in terms of raw specs and performance, but when it comes to software, Apple may take the lead – again, I’ll have to try it for myself.

iPhone Duo vs Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Battery life

Apple doesn’t typically reveal the actual capacity of its batteries, but the iPhone Duo does feature one battery on either side of the device, both working together as one.

The company says you’ll get up to 24 hours of typical use, or up to 31 hours of video playback using the inner display and a whopping 44 hours using the outer display.

Samsung is a little more forthcoming with the numbers. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a 4,800mAh silicon-carbon battery, which Samsung says delivers up to 26 hours of video playback.

It’s difficult to compare Apple and Samsung’s video playback figures directly because they use different testing methodologies, but Apple’s battery claims are huge if true.

( Apple )

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 supports 45W wired charging. It can reach up to 63 per cent in 30 minutes. It also supports 20W wireless charging.

Apple says the iPhone Duo can get to 50 per cent in roughly 20 minutes using a 60W-capable or higher adapter. It also supports MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging, potentially getting to 50 per cent in 30 minutes. Unlike the Galaxy Z Fold 8, the magnets are built directly into the phone, so you don’t need a magnetic case to take advantage of Qi2 charging, though you can charge wirelessly at up to 20W.

iPhone Duo vs Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Price

Neither phone is cheap, but you may gulp when you hear the iPhone Duo’s price.

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is £1,699 for 256GB of storage, £1,869 for 512GB and £2,209 for 1TB. That’s already pretty expensive, but the iPhone Duo makes it sound frankly cheap.

The iPhone Duo starts at £1,999 for the 256GB model, but the 512GB model is an eye-watering £2,199, with the 1TB model costing an enormous £2,599. There’s even a 2TB model for £3,199, which is more expensive than some of the most expensive MacBook Pro laptops and almost as expensive as the Apple Vision Pro.

The Z Fold 8 is more than 1.5mm thinner than the iPhone Duo ( Alex Lee/The Independent )

That means there’s a £300 difference between the entry-level iPhone Duo and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8. The 512GB iPhone Duo costs £330 more than the equivalent Fold 8 and the 1TB model costs £390 more.

Samsung is the obvious winner on price, but £1,699 is still an absurd amount of money for a foldable phone with just two cameras. We’ll see if Apple can justify that £300 premium after testing.

iPhone Duo vs Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Which should you buy?

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is thinner, significantly lighter and £300 cheaper, and Samsung also has years of experience making foldables, which shows in the Z Fold 8’s polish.

But the iPhone Duo looks really compelling. It has a more versatile hinge, better dust protection, a better speaker array and Apple Pencil support. Apple appears to have put a lot of thought into how iOS works over the two displays as well.

For Android users, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the only passport foldable you’ll want to buy, and iPhone users finally have a foldable of their own. If you’re not wedded to either operating system, the iPhone Duo looks a little more exciting. I’ll reserve judgement until I get a chance to review the iPone Duo.

News.title: Trump’s own contractor admits its shoddy work caused the problem at the Reflecting Pool - not vandals
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

The contractor that refurbished the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool acknowledged that its own faulty work — not sabotage — led the newly installed liner to become damaged, according to a new report.

President Donald Trump repeatedly blamed vandals after sections of the liner began peeling away shortly after the president’s multimillion-dollar refurbishment was completed this summer.

“I saw it. They cut it. They cut it very violently,” Trump told reporters in June, alleging that a “box-cutter or a knife of some kind” had caused what he described as a “350-foot slit” in the pool’s lining.

But Atlantic Industrial Coatings, the contractor, told the Trump administration in reports that its design and implementation of the renovation project had fallen short, The New York Times reported. The report was based on government documents, but few specifics were given about them.

For one, the company stated, workers applied too little primer because of “human oversight,” causing the liner’s layers to adhere to one another.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump's contractor admitted that shoddy work caused problems at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, according to a new report ( Reuters )

The “American flag blue” liner also contained two “incompatible” chemicals.

“The chemical on top reached a temperature hotter than what the compound underneath could withstand, and the heat caused the bottom layer to blister and come loose,” the Times reported. “The contractor said it had not expected that outcome because it was very uncommon to mix the two products in that way.”

The report comes after prosecutors, in July, moved to dismiss its cases against several people who had been charged with vandalizing the pool. A filing from U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro’s office stated that the “damage was the result of a botched installation and not vandalism.”​

open image in gallery The Reflecting Pool has faced numerous problems since its renovation including algaee blooms and paint ripping away ( AFP/Getty )

The Reflecting Pool currently remains closed and fenced off. Since Trump announced the repairs, the project has been a boondoggle. The repairs were supposed to be finished by July 4 in time for America’s 250th birthday celebrations, but constant setbacks delayed those plans.

Algae blooms, the paint ripping away and the discolored water were all part of the reported aftermath. The Trump administration tried to blame others, including vandals, for the damage.

"Look what VANDALS did to the grass connecting the vandalized World War II Monument and the vandalized Reflecting Pool, which will be opened again, and better than ever, shortly," Trump said around July 4 also referencing damage to the grass at the national mall.

"Anybody who thinks the Reflecting Pool wasn't vandalized should go back to Law School!" he added.

Pirro’s office charged several people in connection with the alleged vandalism,, then dismissed the case and admitted it did not have the full picture before charging.

Atlantic Industrial Coatings, which the government agreed to pay $14.7 million, plans to undertake the repairs.

“President Trump promised to make D.C. safe and beautiful, and he’s delivering,” a White House spokesperson told the Times, while an Interior Department spokesperson seemed to continue blaming the pool’s problems on vandals.

News.title: Razaullah’s incredible hitting scrambles England’s minds
News.content:
England will look to complete the series whitewash as they hold a commanding position coming into day three of the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston in what could be the final day of the English Test summer.

England finished up their first innings on 453 on day two, with a mammoth 320-run lead over Pakistan. Five England batsmen passed the fifty mark; Emilio Gay, Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence, Jamie Smith and Ollie Robinson, but none went on to convert those half centuries into hundreds. It means that Ben Duckett’s century against New Zealand at Trent Bridge back in June will be the only England Test hundred of the summer, the first time that has happened in a six-Test summer. England managed 21 half centuries over the course of the summer, so it works out as 4.76% conversion rate.

Having seen England pile on the runs, Pakistan then lost a wicket with the first ball of their second innings, with Saim Ayub making a pair to sum up a miserable return to their Test side for the opener having been jettisoned in as part of wholesale changes for the visitors. Abdullah Shafique followed three balls later, with Robinson taking both wickets as his fine summer continued. Robinson now has 28 wickets across four Tests this summer at a staggering average of 7.75. Joe Root made history yesterday, taking his 220th catch, the most by an outfielder in Test history. Rain though prevented England the opportunity of potentially wrapping up a two-day finish in a Test in this country for the first time since 2000.

Pakistan will resume on 52/2, still 268 runs behind England, with Azan Awais resuming on 29 not out and will be joined by Shan Masood, who is on 21. Pakistan are yet to reach 200 or bat more than 51 overs in this series so the series whitewash may not be a million miles away. Will we see any rare Pakistan resistance in this series or will England’s seamers dominate again? Play on day three from Edgbaston is set to get under at 11am and it could be the final day of not just the series but the English Test summer.

News.title: Interest rates predicted to rise four times by July
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Britain’s economy grew unexpectedly in July, handing Chancellor John Healey some breathing space ahead of the Budget.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). Analysts had expected the UK economy to flatline.

Officials said pubs and clubs, advertisers and alcohol makers reported an increase in turnover linked to the World Cup, while many firms also said the second hottest July on record had a positive impact.

The data showed Britain’s economy may be benefitting from the massive investments in AI, with activity in telecoms expanding by 1.1pc in July, computer programming up 3.5pc and information services up 1.1pc.

The data will lend support to the “optimistic story” that John Healey tried to tell about the economy in a major speech this week.

Growth also accelerated from 0.3pc in June after Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July.

It slightly eases pressure on the Chancellor after the cost of government borrowing costs rose to levels not seen in decades after a jump in the price of oil reignited a bond market sell-off.

The Treasury’s 10-year interest rate rose above 5.3pc on Thursday, a level not seen since 2007. It threatens to wipe around £10bn from Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom before his first Budget next month, according to economists at the Item Club. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Badenoch must scrap triple lock, says senior Tory MP | Politician urges Conservatives to ‘slaughter some sacred cows’ to stabilise the public finances

2) | Michael O’Leary demands sacking of ‘incompetent’ air traffic control chief | Ryanair boss urges Transport Secretary to dismiss Martin Rolfe after IT meltdown grounds passengers

3) | Guardian staff threaten walkout over pay as paper hails record revenues | Journalists’ union will ballot members over strike in protest against company’s offer

4) | Hotel bosses criticise Burnham’s fresh assault on hospitality | Prime Minister gives mayors power for unlimited levy on stays in blow for pubs and families

5) | Iceland to become first British supermarket to open in Falklands | New shop will begin trading before Christmas despite rising tensions with Argentina over islands

What happened overnight

Oil prices remained at their highest level since May as tensions flared in the Middle East.

Brent crude was above $105 a barrel after after Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s keyport of Mocha, threatening Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea.

Asian shares declined, tracking Wall Street losses. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8pc to 63,442.30, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3pc to 6,872.39.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped 0.8pc to 24,753.54. The Shanghai Composite index was down 1.8pc to 3,862.73.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.2pc to 8,712.20.

Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.7pc, while India’s Sensex declined 1pc.

On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.6pc in its fourth straight loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6pc, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.7pc.

News.title: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: ‘All I see are dead bodies’: The survivors of Syria’s chemical massacres
News.content:
“Unfortunately, I am still alive,” says Mohammed Suliaiman Abo Alkair, his green eyes heavy and distant.

The 38-year-old steps from his living room onto the roof and gestures towards a cluster of trees – a lone patch of green in a sea of grey rubble. It was there, at two in the morning 13 years ago that the whistle of a rocket ended not in an explosion but a thud.

For a moment, there was relief; the feeling of being spared. But then came a cloud of the nerve agent sarin.

Almost everyone around Mohammed died. His family and one small boy in a neighbouring house were the only ones to survive.

That August night, as Damascus slept, forces loyal to the Syrian President Bashar al-Assad launched eight sarin-filled rockets at the opposition-held districts of Zamalka, Ein Tarma and Jobar. The US government estimated that 1,429 people were killed, including 426 children. Other estimates put the number at 1729.

For more than a decade, nobody was held to account. Mr Assad denied the attack, shielded those responsible and later used sarin again – at Khan Sheikhoun in 2017, and in at least ten further attacks documented by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

Only after Mr Assad fled Syria in December 2024 did the prospect of justice emerge. Investigators for Syria’s new government have since uncovered previously undeclared chemical-munitions caches, and the authorities have detained 18 suspects. None has yet been tried or punished.

But as attention turns at last to justice, the survivors remain invisible, absent from the reckoning. For now at least they remain largely invisible.

News.title: What an AI Armageddon might actually look like
News.content:
Jacob Coxon has left AI developer Anthropic with a public reckoning. For three years, the 27-year-old Brit trained models at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Both AI startups acted irresponsibly, Coxon wrote on X on Wednesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Jacob Coxon warned.

The response from his manager arrived just hours later. Evan Hubinger, Head of Alignment Research at Anthropic, also confirmed the warning: “We are, in fact, earnestly convinced that AI could kill all humans! I think the probability of that happening within the next decade is greater than ten percent.”

Anthropic, he added, does not yet have a solution to this problem.

When the head of safety at a multibillion-dollar technology company casually predicts humanity’s downfall at the hands of his own product, the debate leaves the realm of academic thought experiments.

The warning comes from the engineers writing the code. Both developers point to an industry dynamic in which competitive pressures outweigh safety concerns.

But what exactly are AI developers afraid of? What is the hypothetical scenario in which artificial intelligence brings about Armageddon?

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two-day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three-match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stand in the lead-up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight, but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson, whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline-grabbing stuff. This time it felt almost predictable, even disappointing for those wanting to see some sort of contest.

News.title: ‘At that price, I’d expect it to make me a cup of tea’: Your verdict on Apple’s £2k foldable iPhone
News.content:
Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, was unveiled this week. With a starting price of £1999, it’s £300 more expensive than Samsung’s rival Galaxy Z Fold 8.

Similar in size to a British passport, when closed it’s shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone. Once opened, it resembles a small iPad, allowing the user to open multiple apps at once.

While our reporter, who got a first look at the phone, was impressed by the build quality and functionality, it remains to be seen whether she feels it’s worth the high price.

We asked Telegraph readers their initial thoughts on the iPhone Duo and, as well as their opinions on Apple products and how often they upgrade.

Sports.title: Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, 34, charged with assaulting wife as ex-Premier League star set for trial
Sports.content:
Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, 34, charged with assaulting wife as ex-Premier League star set for trial

Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, who played for Cardiff City in the Premier League, attended Magistrates Court where he learned his trial date

View 3 Images Nathaniel Mendez-Laing now plays for MK Dons (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

MK Dons player Nathaniel Mendez-Laing has appeared in court, where he has denied claims he assaulted his wife.

‌



The former Premier League ace stands accused of attacking his wife, Saira Mendez-Laing, while they were in their home in Shenstone, Staffordshire. The incident was alleged to have taken place in June.

‌



He was arrested and charged with assault by beating after the police were called to their house. In magistrates' court on Friday September 11, he denied one count of assault by beating.

‌



Mendez-Laing was on crutches as he arrived wearing a black suit with white shirt. During his appearance at Cannock magistrates' court, he only confirmed his name, age and address.

In August, it's understood the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) authorised charges.

View 3 Images Nathaniel Mendez-Laing appeared in magistrates' court (Image: Instagram)

‌



The MK Dons ace was freed on conditional bail by the court. This was granted by District Judge Joseph O'Connor, who also stated the player will stand trial next January.

Mendez-Laing made 20 Premier League appearances for Cardiff City, where he contributed four goals and one assist.

He now plays for the Dons in League One, having moved to the club from Derby County last summer. While he was born in Birmingham, he is a Guatemala international.

‌



He qualifies for the Central American country, who he has amassed 20 caps with, as both his mother and grand mother hail from the Latin American nation.

View 3 Images Mendez-Laing played in the Premier League with Cardiff City (Image: 2018 AMA Sports Photo Agency)

The player chose to represent Guatemala having previously made appeared for the England U17s when he was a youngster.

Article continues below

Throughout his career, the wide midfielder has also represented Wolverhampton Wanderers, Peterborough, Sheffield United, Portsmouth, Shrewsbury, Cambridge United, Rochdale, Middlesbrough and Sheffield Wednesday.

Mendez-Lain and Saira married in June last year. After they tied the knot, the Dons uploaded a congratulatory post on the club's social media accounts.

His club have said they will not comment on ongoing legal proceedings.

Sports.title: Man Utd disadvantage brushed off by Enzo Maresca ahead of derby - 'It happens in football'
Sports.content:
Man Utd disadvantage brushed off by Enzo Maresca ahead of derby - 'It happens in football'

Manchester United will host neighbours Manchester City having played in midweek, but the Red Devils' game was two days later than their rivals

View 2 Images Man City have enjoyed two days more rest time ahead of the Manchester derby

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca insists Manchester United "are going to be ready" despite them having 48 hours less preparation time for Sunday's derby.

The two rivals come together at Old Trafford this weekend in what is a first major test for both sides - and both teams come into the match off the back of wins to kick off their Champions League campaign.

City won 2-0 at Porto on Tuesday evening before United hammered Sabah 4-0 on Thursday - meaning Michael Carrick's side have less recovery and preparation time than their opponents.

But Maresca has referenced a similar scenario last season, which saw City as the ones with the reduced preparation time. It came before they faced Arsenal this time last year, but the Gunners had faced Athletic Bilbao on the Tuesday whilst City took on Napoli on the Thursday.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Maresca told BBC Sport: "To be honest, the club mentioned to me that it happened exactly the same last year when the club played Napoli and then, after two days, played Arsenal. Sometimes it happens in football. I don't have any doubt that Man United are going to be ready for that. It just matters to adapt."

When pushed on how Michael Carrick would look to use his resources with a turnaround of less than 73 hours, the City boss simply said: "That's a question for Michael. The only thing I can say is it happened and you need to adapt."

Last season former City boss Pep Guardiola joked he was taking his players "hiking in the mountains" so that they could suitably prepare for the game at Emirates Stadium, which they later drew 1-1 after Gabriel Martinelli scored an equaliser in injury time.

View 2 Images Man Utd made light work of Sabah on Thursday night (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

City head to Old Trafford, where they were beaten 2-0 last season in the first game of the Carrick era, with a 100 percent record after three games.

United meanwhile were denied the win at Everton by a stoppage time strike from Ainsley Maitland-Niles. It was the third game in succession that the Red Devils had conceded twice as questions remain over the team's defence.

"We know we have to put in a really good performance and do a lot of good things to get the result we want," said Carrick.

Sports.title: Arsenal enter cost review as 'consultants hired' just months after Premier League title win
Sports.content:
Arsenal enter cost review as 'consultants hired' just months after Premier League title win

Premier League champions Arsenal are conducting a cost review after bringing in a management consultancy firm following one of the best seasons in their history

View 2 Images Arsenal are continuing to review after winning the Premier League (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal have brought in outside consultants to examine the club's internal operations and identify areas for improvement. The move comes months after they won their first Premier League title in 22 years and reached just the second Champions League final in club history.

‌



They have also won their first three matches of this season, only trailing league leaders Manchester City by goals scored. The Gunners, though, are seemingly unwilling to stand still and rest on their laurels off the pitch.

‌



Sky News has reported that Arsenal have enlisted management consultancy firm Boston Consulting Group (BCG) to scrutinise their balance sheets as part of a wide-ranging cost review.

‌



Their chief executive, Richard Garlick, is understood to be taking a central role in the assessment of the club, which employs around 800 members of staff.

The process is said to be ongoing, meaning no firm decisions have yet been reached - though the review is reported to concentrate on the 'non-footballing aspects' of the club.

That being said, a financial review does not necessarily signal impending redundancies. A review last season also saw the overhaul of their medical department. Reach PLC approached Arsenal, but the club declined to comment on the matter.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal want to continue improving (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal splashed out significantly in the transfer market, yet ranked only ninth among the Premier League's biggest net-spenders. The marquee arrivals were Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United and Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa.

North London also witnessed record-breaking sales, with Gabriel Martinelli becoming the club's most expensive departure when he sealed a move to Al-Hilal for £60m. Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard were also offloaded to Barcelona and Besiktas, respectively, fetching a combined £28.1m.

‌



Arsenal's triumphant campaign last season generated approximately £300m for the club. This sum comprises prize money earned from clinching the title, reaching the Champions League final, the League Cup final and the FA Cup quarter-final.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

In May, sources close to Arsenal informed our sister site, football.london, that the club's ownership, headed up by Stan Kroenke's son Josh, are determined to make the club financially self-sustaining while maintaining success on the pitch.

‌



At the final home fixture of the season, Josh Kroenke penned a letter to supporters, stating: "The connection we feel with our supporters fills us with pride. Between us, we are building something very special and, wherever this month of May takes us, there will be no standing still when the season ends.

"We are always forward in our approach, taking the learnings as we go and relentless in the pursuit of progress. We remain focused on raising the standard, creating the best possible environment for our players and people to succeed, and elevating the unity that exists between club and community."

Arsenal's blistering start to the new campaign hints that further glory could be on the horizon. The Gunners boast a perfect winning record across all competitions so far, having thrashed Manchester City 3-0 to claim the Community Shield, edged past Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium, and secured a 1-0 away triumph over Napoli in the Champions League.

Article continues below

Mikel Arteta's side head north to take on Sunderland at the Stadium of Light, before kicking off their League Cup campaign with an away fixture against Ipswich Town next Tuesday.

Sports.title: Liverpool vs Fulham - eight players to miss Anfield clash including £85m ace
Sports.content:
Liverpool vs Fulham - eight players to miss Anfield clash including £85m ace

It will be a Liverpool reunion for Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa, but things are not going to be easy for him, and Reds boss Andoni Iraola

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo is one player who will be absent for Liverpool (Image: Justin Setterfield, Getty Images)

Eight players will be missing when Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa reunites with his former side Liverpool at Anfield. The former Reds defender takes his team to Merseyside in desperate need of a positive result.

Fulham have been defeated in all three of their Premier League matches, losing to Chelsea, Sunderland and Crystal Palace. Meanwhile, Liverpool are gathering momentum under Iraola.

They easily beat Ipswich Town 2-0 in their last Premier League match, before overcoming Atletico Madrid 2-1 in the Champions League. It's a big contest for both sides, who share a lengthy list of absentees. Mirror Football take a look at who will be missing for both sides.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool

The primary concern for Liverpool centres on the fitness of Cody Gakpo. The forward sat out the victory over Atletico and faces a late fitness assessment ahead of the Fulham fixture.

"Cody we will see. He didn't train yesterday," Iraola said. "Today we will try with him and let's see if he's ready for tomorrow or we need to wait for the next one."

Should he fail to prove his fitness, he will join defender Joe Gomez on the treatment table. The England man sustained an injury during pre-season and has yet to return to the first-team squad.

While he is edging closer to a comeback, this weekend's fixture may arrive too soon for him. Federico Chiesa is also anticipated to be unavailable having picked up a muscle injury in the latter stages of pre-season. There is currently no indication of when he will make his return.

Three further longer-term injury concerns remain sidelined, with Giovani Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike all continuing their respective rehabilitation programmes.

In an encouraging boost for Iraola, he has confirmed that summer signing Bradley Barcola is expected to be fit after being substituted with cramp during the victory over Atletico. "We still need to train this afternoon. Barcola was just cramps. We have to evaluate how he is today, but there's no injury. He should, I think, be available, if everything goes normal."

Fulham

Fulham have relatively little to concern themselves with on the injury front, with just two players expected to sit out the match. Club captain Tom Cairney will be absent as he continues his recovery from a minor knee procedure last month.

Young striker Jonah Kusi-Asare is yet to feature in any matchday squad this season. He has made 10 first-team appearances for the club, and was hampered by a knee injury last season.

View 2 Images Arbeloa has endured a difficult start to life at Fulham (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The match will pit Arbeloa against Iraola, a man he knows well from their time together in Spain. "I played with Andoni in the national team, and obviously we faced each other many, many times in La Liga.

"I know him very, very well. I saw him when he was the coach of Mirandés, Rayo Vallecano, and after in Bournemouth, so I know that he's an amazing coach, and I'm not surprised that now he's the coach of Liverpool.

"He has been doing amazing work here in the Premier League, and now in Liverpool you can see they are playing in the style that he's always playing with his teams, and of course it will be so difficult for us tomorrow."

Sports.title: Michail Antonio returns to English football nearly two years after brutal car crash
Sports.content:
Michail Antonio returns to English football nearly two years after brutal car crash

Michail Antonio spent a period with Qatari side Al-Sailiya following his exit from West Ham after his devastating car crash but the Jamaican forward has now made a return to English football

View 2 Images Michail Antonio has finally found his next club (Image: Getty Images)

Michail Antonio has penned a one-year deal with Watford to make his return to English football. The former West Ham star has been without a club since leaving Qatari side Al-Sailiya in the summer.

‌



Antonio, now 36, had been in the Middle East for a brief spell having been a free agent following a devastating car crash in December 2024.

‌



Speaking after his move was made official, Antonio said: “It’s a good set of boys here. They are focused and ready to show their abilities this season.

‌



“Watford is a big club and hopefully I can come in and bring success and help wherever I can. I’ve scored a few goals against Watford! So hopefully I can score some for Watford now when I’m fully up to speed."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Antonio could make his debut for his new club this weekend as Watford come up against Stoke City at Vicarage Road. The Hornets currently sit 12th in the Championship after six games.

Antonio’s move signals his first return to English football following his exit from West Ham. Prior to that, he was involved in a car crash in December 2024, and was close to losing his life.

Speaking to the BBC about the crash, Antonio said: "It's weird, because the whole way through this, I have been told that I was awake and was speaking to everybody - the police, the people, and the person who found me.

‌



"My leg was completely shattered and they got me out and put a splint on it by the side of the car. Everyone believed I got an air ambulance out, but the helicopter couldn't get off the ground because of the storm, so I was driven to the hospital."

View 2 Images Michail Antonio has not made an appearance in English football since leaving West Ham (Image: Getty Images)

On seeing the wreckage of his car, he added: "It gave me a weird feeling in my stomach. It just made me realise how close I was to dying. I had seen the pictures but it was 10 times worse in person. The car was an absolute mess. It was difficult for me."

Article continues below

Antonio has represented Reading, Cheltenham Town, Southampton, Colchester United, Sheffield Wednesday and Nottingham Forest throughout his career. He joined West Ham in 2015 and went on to score 83 goals in 323 appearances for the Hammers, while he helped the side to the Conference League title in 2023.

Antonio was previously close to moves to both Leicester City and Brentford over the past year but neither side agreed a deal with the Jamaican international.

Sports.title: Chelsea transfer target Lamine Camara speaks out on failed deadline day move
Sports.content:
Chelsea transfer target Lamine Camara speaks out on failed deadline day move

Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara was on the verge of a deadline day switch to Chelsea this summer only to see the rug pulled from beneath his feet and the move cancelled

View 2 Images Lamine Camara saw a deadline day switch to Chelsea collapse (Image: Getty Images)

Lamine Camara insists he is trying to put his failed move to Chelsea behind him. The Monaco midfielder looked to be on the verge of a deadline day switch to Stamford Bridge this summer.

‌



The Blues had agreed a deal with the Ligue 1 side on the final day of the window, with a £47m move in place. But the deal fell through at the 11th hour, with Monaco in no mood to sell due to Folarin Balogun’s expected switch to Everton - albeit that move fell apart as well.

‌



Camara has now spoken out on the failed Premier League switch for the first time and is keen to move on. He said: “It was a somewhat turbulent and difficult time.

‌



“But that’s part of a player’s life. I tried to remain professional, avoid dwelling on it, and move on so I could quickly focus on the upcoming match in Paris (September 4, a 2–1 win). Once it was over, there was no point thinking about it.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He added: “Did I want to go to Chelsea? Saying that now would imply I’m no longer fully present with the team. Yes, there was a possibility I might leave, but it didn’t happen at the last minute. These things happen. Look at the example of Julian Alvarez with Atlético Madrid. It happens all over the world, and I’m trying to turn the page as quickly as possible to focus on the season.

“If it doesn’t come back around, it will be because I gave up or didn’t work hard enough. If I keep going like this, I know I can help the team perform well. Football moves fast, and perhaps other chances will arise. But for now, I’m staying focused on the season.”

Camara was intended to be a direct replacement for Enzo Fernandez, with the Argentine completing a big-money switch to Manchester City.

‌



Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro gave his take on the move in the days after the window closed. He said: "We started to open negotiations with Chelsea for Lamine. I informed the player directly myself. I called him.

View 2 Images Camara was seen as a potential replacement for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Getty Images)

“I informed his agent as we always do. Very open. We had discussions between the conditions for Lamine to go to Chelsea. At the same time, the medical discussion was ongoing with Balo. And what happened was that around 10:00pm in our time here, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that okay, there's no problem. We are ready to do let's sign the contract.

‌



"Chelsea was always testing and trying. 'What about Lamine? What about Lamine?' I've been talking to them from the last 10 days. As soon as we got the information, yes, we did came back to Chelsea and told 'okay, we have our deal there'.

"There is no deal on Lamine because it's also fair to do this. It's also part of the game. There's no reason that this kind of discussions or dynamic on the last day of the transfer window which all of us decided to be on the last day trying to find solutions with the clock ticking in our neck that now this kind of interaction becomes the bad guys in the room that Monaco is not fair, Monaco is not right. Everybody is very fair and nice in football industry just Monaco is not too much. So this is the storytelling.

"We informed again everyone that there was no deal with Chelsea. We progressed. Premier League has a mechanism which you can request one extra hour to finish the paperwork. This was done five minutes to close the transfer window there for us to finish all the paperwork between Monaco and Everton and Balo. I signed the contract. Everton signed the contract.

Article continues below

"At the last moment the player decided not to sign and basically the allegation of Balo is that 'I'm not feeling well by the way the club treated me. I'm not feeling well'. By the way, the medical department of Everton brought doubts about my future or my healthy. I have nothing. So, I'm not comfortable to sign a loan contract here. And that's the way we finish our transfer window."

Sports.title: Man Utd confirm 685 season ticket bans as touting investigation sparks furious backlash
Sports.content:
Man Utd confirm 685 season ticket bans as touting investigation sparks furious backlash

Manchester United have announced the results of their controversial investigation into ticket touting at Old Trafford, which has sparked a planned protest this weekend

View 3 Images Manchester United fans have criticised the club's investigation (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

Manchester United have removed 685 season tickets following a lengthy and much-criticised investigation into touting at Old Trafford.

‌



Back in August, the club identified 1,617 accounts exhibiting "unusual activity". The holders of those accounts were then contacted and asked to provide explanations for the activity that was deemed suspicious.

‌



This heavy-handed approach sparked a furious backlash among supporters, with many believing that innocent and loyal fans were unfairly being accused. A protest ahead of Sunday's Manchester Derby at Old Trafford has been called over what fan group The 1958 said were sanctions being made without "compelling evidence".

‌



United have now announced the results of their investigation, which allowed fans to appeal to an independent appeals panel. The club said 685 season tickets were revoked, including 499 whereby a ban was upheld by the appeals panel.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Meanwhile, 468 cases were resolved after the season ticket holder provided information to exonerate themselves. The club have admitted they "did not anticipate the extent" to which fans shared account details "in circumstances they regarded as legitimate" and in those cases no sanctions were imposed.

The club said in a statement: "Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain. This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts.

"These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United.

‌



"Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list."

View 3 Images Manchester United fans are unhappy with the way the touting investigation was carried out (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

The club added: "We want to allow any sanctioned ticket holder the opportunity to refer their case to the Independent Football Ombudsman. Therefore, we will wait until after the international break before reallocating season tickets.

‌



"Any seats used on a match-by-match basis before then will be sold at season ticket prices, not matchday prices. The club is not profiting from this process."

The club said 226 accounts received final warnings for breaking rules but not for financial gain, while 238 accounts guilty of further abuses saw their initial season ticket ban reduced to a ban on home ticket forwarding and away match applications.

Speaking before the club's announcement on Friday, Chris Rumfitt, a spokesperson for Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST), summed up the ill feeling among fans.

‌



He told Mirror Football: "If it was a clampdown on touting we would be entirely supportive, because the biggest losers of touting are fans who get exploited and ripped off.

View 3 Images Ticket prices have been another bone of contention (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

"But what they are calling a clampdown on touting has brought up a huge numbers of match-going fans doing ordinary things match-going fans do, i.e. passing tickets between groups of friends at face value, which people wouldn't consider to be touting.

‌



"There is no question that large number of ordinary fans have been caught up in this because what the club has defined as 'suspicious' included lots of things fans do."

Rumfitt believes the issue has touched such a nerve with supporters that only the botched attempt to form a European Super League five years ago compares to the strength of feeling in the stands.

He added: "The approach the club has taken has been 'ban first, ask questions later'. They've banned people and then asked them to prove that they haven't done anything wrong, which isn't normally how things work in this country. The burden of proof works the other way around.

Article continues below

"There's a massive amount of discontent among all fan groups, it's really united the fans. The way the club has gone about this is completely wrong. It has spread further mistrust."

Sports.title: Mumtaz: Razaullah wrote 'perfect chapter' to revive reeling Pakistan
Sports.content:
Former Pakistan captain Urooj Mumtaz lauded youngster Razaullah and said he wrote the "perfect chapter" to revive his reeling side after his sensational 81 off 63 balls against England on day three at Edgbaston.

Razaullah, who has only played eight previous first-class matches in his career, smacked nine sixes in his remarkable innings, equalling Tim Southee's record for the most maximums for a Test debutant, dazzling in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42) that eventually propelled Pakistan to a total of 449 and set England a target of 130.

The 21-year-old consolidated an already impressive performance on debut with the ball, taking four wickets in England's innings, including that of skipper Joe Root for his first.

His performance with the bat was undoubtedly the deciding factor in forcing the match into a fourth day that looked so improbable when he arrived at the crease, when Pakistan trailed by two runs at 318-8.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Razaullah smashed nine sixes to equal Tim Southee’s record for the most by a player on Test debut during a remarkable innings against England at Edgbaston.

"His innings was simply sensational," Mumtaz said on Sky Sports. "A perfectly written first chapter of his Test career. All that passion, the flair of Pakistan cricket!

"One 21-year-old who wasn't even on the list gets on the plane and gets his baggy green. Then Joe Root is his first Test wicket, he takes a four-fer on debut, and makes 81, with nine sixes.

"All of Edgbaston and all of Pakistan were on their feet!"

'Razaullah showed the beauty of Pakistan's raw talent'

Image: Razaullah equalled Tim Southee's record for most sixes on Test debut with nine

Mumtaz praised the spirit that Razaullah embodied, especially in the face of an off-field crisis that saw seven changes to the tourists' squad and a head coach axed ahead of the third Test after two heavy losses to begin the series.

"He showed the beauty of Pakistan and their raw talent - even he doesn't know what he's capable of!

"He's come off the plane and has absolutely no baggage. Yes he has a first-class hundred in dramatic fashion, but his hand speed is so quick he is ripping through the ball.

"He sits so deep in the crease and barely any of his boundaries are mishits - all of his sixes were monsters.

"That's the spark, the energy, the exuberance of youth that you are looking for.

"There was a smile on his face and he was not overwhelmed by the occasion. He didn't look in awe of it - he almost looked like he believed."

Razaullah: I just had to bat - you got to enjoy it!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain labelled Pakistan’s selection of Saim Ayub as a ‘disrespect for Test Match cricket’ after they flew out the batsman for his first class game in 11 months, just 10 days after playing in the CPL.

Pakistan debutant Razaullah, using Urooj Mumtaz' translations after speaking to Sky Sports in Urdu:

"I just had to bat, you are the ones who get to enjoy it!

"I was planning to take it longer and deeper - 81 runs is not bad though!

"The ball was in my slot - I was eyeing that up and trying to provide support for the other batters and trying to take it as deep as possible - I broke both my bats and wore down my third.

"There was no point at which I didn't enjoy it or when I was scared.

"I was wanting the strike, and overall I wanted to keep the strike as long as possible to get Pakistan another day."

Do Pakistan have any chance?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence produced a stunning catch at slip off Gus Atkinson to dismiss Shan Masood for 95, denying the Pakistan batter a century at Edgbaston.

Mumtaz praised the role of fellow tail-ender Abbas - who notched his highest-ever Test score - in the partnership, and refused to rule out a miraculous comeback for Pakistan:

"A perfect script.

"To put one youngster in to bat with one stalwart of the game in Mohammed Abbas who is now on the honours board at Lord's after an eight-year gap between fifers," Mumtaz added.

"Abbas said 'I'm not just a seam bowler - I'm going to hit a few down the ground,' and he did!

"It all just amalgamates to show what could have happened if Pakistan had the temperament, the flair and the technique to back it up for the twelve-odd days of cricket we've had.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports Cricket team analyse a remarkable third day at Edgbaston as Pakistan fought back from a huge first-innings deficit, with debutant Razaullah’s explosive 81 helping set England 130 to complete a 3-0 series sweep.

"If anyone is a betting person, after what's happened today, it's almost like that dimming light has been ignited again.

"You never know [what will happen]. Razaullah had a four-fer on debut [in England's first innings], and he provides a point of difference with pace.

"They'll have to believe - there will have to be words of wisdom - and also know that there's not too much to be said.

"They can leave it at that, watch some tapes and come back tomorrow with hope."

Sports.title: Will it be a Sabalenka 'three-peat' or maiden US Open for new No 1 Rybakina?
Sports.content:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka is looking to become the first woman to achieve the 'three-peat' in New York since Serena Williams in 2014 but she faces incoming world No 1 Elena Rybakina in the US Open final on Saturday.

Rybakina's results this year, starting with her Australian Open final triumph against Sabalenka, will see her rise to the top of the rankings on Monday, ending the Belarussian's 99-week reign.

But Sabalenka can exact some revenge for both that defeat and being overtaken at the WTA summit by defending her US Open title against Rybakina in Saturday's Flushing Meadows final - live on Sky Sports Tennis from 5pm.

Sabalenka is now 36-3 in the last five years at the US Open

"I really understand about how tough it is to reach the world No 1," said Sabalenka.

"It's a lot of work and, yeah, that was one of my goals, but right now there was not much I could do. I didn't really perform well in the middle of the season.

"Elena took it over and played really well. But I can only focus on myself and just stay in the moment and trying to do my best right now just so I keep it tight - and maybe I will take it back from her.

"But, yeah, it does feel a little bit weird. You can perform well in the tournament but still lose the number one position. So it's OK. It's sport. I love that. That's the beauty of sport, right? Like, everyone chasing everyone, and it's all about little things that you improve and you get better at."

A mouth-watering final between the two top seeds

"It's an important match, and since it's a final, it's honestly, I feel like it doesn't matter who is on the other side. You just want to win and do your best," said Rybakina, the first player from Kazakhstan to reach world No 1.

"But also, I don't want to put too much pressure on myself because we are all very close in the ranking.

"Even if something goes wrong in the final, I still have other opportunities, other tournaments until the end of the year.

"We push each other when we play these matches, and you clearly can see on what you need to work more. I think that's great that you play against someone who pushes you till the limits."

Sports.title: Remarkable Razaullah knock denies England series sweep inside three days
Sports.content:
England were denied a series sweep of Pakistan inside three days of the final Test at Edgbaston after a remarkable display of six-hitting from 21-year-old Razaullah late on Friday.

Pakistan enjoyed easily their finest day of what's otherwise been a dismal series but were still trailing by two when their eighth wicket fell early into the evening session, only for Razaullah to smash 81 off just 63 deliveries, clearing the ropes a staggering nine times to equal Tim Southee's record for a debutant.

He shared in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42), who himself hit two sixes before picking out point off Josh Tongue in the closing overs, while Razaullah's fun was finally ended - and the day's play - as he was stumped off Dan Lawrence (2-17).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Razaullah smashed nine sixes to equal Tim Southee’s record for the most by a player on Test debut during a remarkable innings against England at Edgbaston

England, guilty of losing the plot in the final session, will now look to chase down 130 on day four, a far stiffer target than initially looked likely, albeit one they should still reel in to clinch a first ever home series whitewash of Pakistan.

Score summary - England vs Pakistan, third Test, Edgbaston Pakistan 133 all out in 33.5 overs in first innings (put in to bat): Saud Shakeel (43), Mohammad Abbas (21); Josh Tongue (4-42), Ollie Robinson (3-15), Jofra Archer (3-25) England 453 all out in 89 overs in first innings: Harry Brook (75), Jamie Smith (69), Dan Lawrence (65), Emilio Gay (60), Ollie Robinson (50); Razaullah (4-148) Pakistan 449 all out in 96.4 overs in second innings (lead by 129): Shan Masood (95), Razaullah (81 off 63 balls), Babar Azam (76), Azan Awais (59); Gus Atkinson (3-109)

The tourists might be cursing not testing England further, with Shan Masood (95) and Babar Azam (76) both spurning golden opportunities to score the first century of the series.

While Masood can count himself a touch unfortunate, out to a screamer of a catch by Lawrence - one-handed, diving low to his right in the slips - Babar's dismissal was much more of a head-scratcher, the captain walking straight into an obvious short-ball trap set by England on the stroke of tea.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence produced a stunning catch at slip off Gus Atkinson to dismiss Shan Masood for 95, denying the Pakistan batter a century at Edgbaston

That wicket had seemed to signal the end of the Pakistan resistance, with four wickets falling for 40 runs before Razaullah very much had other plans and pushed things into a fourth day with some almighty swings of the bat.

Resuming the third morning on 52-2, the visitors had been watchful to start, with only 15 runs added from a rather sedate opening 7.2 overs, before they suddenly sparked into life and smashed 117 off the next 20 - the wicket of Azan Awais (59) to a feathered edge down leg off Lawrence the only blot on their morning's work.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence claimed England’s first wicket of day three as Azan Awais fell for 59 following a successful Joe Root review and sharp catch from Jordan Cox

England's four-pronged pace attack hadn't experienced such a session of toil this series without reward, but were improved after the lunch interval, with Gus Atkinson's initial eight-over burst particularly impressive as he finally secured his second wicket of the series, Masood undone by Lawrence's brilliance in the slips.

Babar was Pakistan's next bright hope for a hundred, what would have been his first in Test cricket for almost four years, but England turned to Jofra Archer and Tongue for a bit of bouncer theory and Babar simply couldn't resist taking it on despite repeated warnings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jordan Cox takes a superb catch to dismiss Babar Azam in Edgbaston

It was Tongue (2-106) who finally got his man, Babar gloving one behind, while Archer (1-120) accounted for Saud Shakeel (29) soon after the tea break with another brute of a short ball that he could only balloon to short-leg.

A couple of terrific catches from Jordan Cox behind the stumps then accounted for debutants Ghazi Ghori (16) and Mohammad Imran (4) as Atkinson (3-109) located their inside and outside edges, respectively.

But Pakistan's third debutant, Razaullah, having already impressed with the ball - claiming four first-innings wickets, including that of England's leading Test run-scorer Joe Root in his first over - put on yet another show with an extraordinary display of ball-striking to not only see his side into a lead, but a 129-run advantage at that.

Beyond even his boundary-clearing blitz, there was terrific drama late on when he had an lbw decision against Lawrence overturned on review, only for him to perish the very next ball and what would prove to be the last of the day.

Razaullah: I just had to bat and get Pakistan another day

Razaullah, speaking to Sky Sports Cricket after his 81 off 63 balls:

Image: Razaullah laughs with Mohammad Ali in the midst of his magnificent innings on the third evening at Edgbaston

"I just had to bat, you are the ones who got to enjoy it.

"I was planning to take it longer and deeper - 81 runs is not bad though.

"I was just trying to provide support for the other batters and trying to take it as deep as possible.

"There was no point at which I didn't enjoy it or when I was scared.

"I won't give any messages to the batters - they can do their bit - but I really, really enjoyed it.

"I was wanting the strike, and overall I wanted to keep the strike as long as possible to get Pakistan another day."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports Cricket team analyse a remarkable third day at Edgbaston as Pakistan fought back from a huge first-innings deficit, with debutant Razaullah’s explosive 81 helping set England 130 to complete a 3-0 series sweep

Urooj: Razaullah provided spark | 'Pakistan have to believe'

Sky Sports Cricket's Urooj Mumtaz:

"That was simply sensational. A perfectly written first chapter of his Test career. All that passion, the flair of Pakistan cricket.

"One 21-year-old who wasn't even on the [squad] list gets on the plane and gets his baggy green - Joe Root is his first Test wicket, a four-for on debut, and then 81 with nine sixes - all of Edgbaston and all of Pakistan were on their feet.

"He's come off the plane and has absolutely no baggage. That's the spark, the energy, the exuberance of youth that you are looking for.

"There was a smile on his face and he was not overwhelmed by the occasion. He didn't look in awe of it - he almost looked like he believed.

"If anyone is a betting person, after what's happened today, it's almost like that dimming light has been ignited again.

"You never know. Razaullah provides Pakistan a point of difference with pace, and they'll have to believe."
